# Fixtures

Each folder here is the input of one build, and is checked against the rules of [docs/BEHAVIOUR.md](../../docs/BEHAVIOUR.md) that name it.

- `input-files`: which files are read, with `.ghg-ignore` files in several folders, hidden files and folders, files of other types, and a `.gitignore` and an `.ignore` file that must have no effect.
- `constructs`: every construct of Gherkin in one feature, and a feature in Portuguese.
- `doc-strings`: doc strings with and without a media type, with both delimiters and their escapes, and with uneven indentation.
- `unreadable`: files that cannot be read, beside one that can and one a `.ghg-ignore` rule leaves out, to check that every problem is reported, sorted by path. Its build is meant to fail.
- `anchors`: names that try every part of the anchor rule: gaps, apostrophes, letters outside a to z, a name in NFD, combining marks and joiners, an emoji with its variation selector, unnamed blocks, names that leave nothing, repeats, a scenario named as its feature, and outline rows, with examples that have only a header or no table; a feature in Portuguese, and one in Gherkin's emoji language.
- `highlighting`: steps with every part highlighting finds, and every near miss: quoted parameters with escapes, empty and unclosed, single quotes, placeholders inside and outside outlines and parameters, and numbers inside and outside words, with signs, points and commas, in a background, a scenario, an outline and a rule; and `destaque.feature`, in Portuguese, whose keywords are highlighted as written. Its `ghg.toml` sets both accent colours and builds the pages into `expected`, which are committed; `cargo xtask build` writes them again, to be read before they are committed.
- `configuration`: the command line and `ghg.toml`, one folder per case, each run as the current folder. `default` has no `ghg.toml` and reads the default input. `configured` names its input, beside a `features` folder that would fail, and has a second file in `ci` whose input is relative to its own folder, and a third in `nested` with no `input`, whose default is relative to its own folder too. `mistaken` has unknown keys and a wrong type, `not-boolean` a wrong type for `allow_unnamed`, `empty-input` an empty path, `not-toml` is not valid TOML, `accents` sets both accent colours, `not-colour` gives accents that are not colours, `faint-accents` accents with too little contrast, `mistaken-tags` has a mistake in each table of `tag_links`, beside `list.toml`, whose `tag_links` is not a list of tables, and `mistaken-pages` has a problem with each key of pages. `unnamed` sets `allow_unnamed = false` over features with unnamed blocks, and `unnamed-allowed` has the same features, read with the default and with `allowed.toml`, which sets it to `true`.
- `pages`: features built into pages, compared with the sites committed beside them: `expected`, built with `ghg.toml`, which sets a title and a source link, and `expected-collapsed`, built with `collapsed.toml`, which starts rules, scenarios and backgrounds collapsed and the folder tree hidden. Each site has its folder tree's data, `assets/tree.json`. Its features have tags, descriptions, backgrounds, rules, an unnamed rule, an outline with a named and an unnamed examples block, an outline inside a rule, whose examples are `h4` and whose examples as scenarios hold `h5` headings, data tables with an escaped `|`, doc strings with and without a media type, text that must be escaped, a feature in Portuguese whose file name has spaces and a letter outside a to z, one in Gherkin's emoji language, a doc string that starts with a blank line, and a `.story` file read through a `.ghg-ignore` rule, with no scenarios. Its `outlines.feature` holds outlines whose examples are shown as scenarios: placeholders in steps, data tables, doc strings and a media type, a placeholder no column names, two examples blocks whose rows are counted together, columns that share a name, a value that is itself a placeholder, an outline without a name, and one whose examples have no row. Its folders make folder pages: `billing`, with a feature and a subfolder, `billing/archive`, whose feature has a rule and no scenario and a file name with a space and a `#`, `reports`, with only a subfolder, and `notes`, with no feature file and so no page. After a change to the pages, `cargo run -- build --config tests/fixtures/pages/ghg.toml`, and again with `collapsed.toml`, writes the expected sites again, to be read before they are committed. Each expected site holds the marker of a site without versions, `ghg-site.json`, as every build writes it, and `keep.toml` sets `replace_existing_version = false`, to check that an earlier build is kept.
- `backgrounds`: scenarios that start with backgrounds, built into two sites: `expected`, with `ghg.toml`, in the inline form, and `expected-linked`, with `linked.toml`, which sets `inline_backgrounds = false`. Its features have a feature's background with a data table and a doc string, a rule with a background of its own and one without, a feature in Portuguese where only a rule has a background, a background without steps, a background with no scenario, and a feature with no background. After a change to the pages, `cargo run -- build --config tests/fixtures/backgrounds/ghg.toml`, and again with `linked.toml`, writes the expected sites again.
- `tags`: features built into a site with its tag pages, compared with `expected`, built with `ghg.toml`, which links tags to other sites with groups by number and by name, a `$$`, a pattern whose text comes out empty, and a second pattern this fixture's tags never reach. Its tags are written on features, rules, scenarios and examples blocks, and include two that differ only in case, `@index`, `@needs:db`, tags that leave nothing after the anchor rule, one with letters outside a to z and characters an address must encode, a feature in Portuguese whose file name has spaces, a feature with no scenarios, and a rule with none. After a change, `cargo run -- build --config tests/fixtures/tags/ghg.toml` writes the expected site again.
- `tags-folder`: a feature whose page would be in the folder of the tag pages, beside one that is fine. Its build is meant to fail.
- `same-page`: `a.feature` and `a.story`, read through a `.ghg-ignore` rule, whose pages would have the same path, beside a file that cannot be parsed, and `index.feature` and `sub/Index.story`, whose pages would be a folder's, and `steps.feature`, whose page would be the page of step sentences. Names that differ only in case, of files and of folders, are checked by the service's own tests, since they cannot share a folder in a checkout on every system. Its build is meant to fail.
- `versions`: the output folder of a versioned site, the suites built into it, and a configuration whose `version_name` cannot be a version name, in `bad-name`. `output` holds a development version, `main`, a release, `v1.0.0`, with pages of an earlier build, a pre-release, `v2.0.0-rc.1`, a folder of other files, `docs`, with no marker, and a versions page; the tests that change it work on a copy. `suite` is a feature that builds, with `keep.toml`, which sets `replace_existing_version = false`, and `broken` one that does not. `expected/index.html` is the versions page of `output` once `suite` is built into it as `v1.0.0`.
- `serve`: `ghg serve`. `site` is a site as it is served, with pages in folders, the script, the stylesheet and the shared data a site has, a file with no extension and one whose name needs percent-encoding, served with `--no-build`. `built` is an input with its `ghg.toml`, which the tests copy where they can change it, to build, watch and rebuild. `reload` is a feature with many long scenarios, ending with an outline whose examples as scenarios start collapsed, so that their headings are hidden, for `tests/browser/reload.mjs`, which checks in Chromium, with Playwright, that a reload keeps the reader's heading; the browser check, `cargo xtask check-browser`, runs it.
- `accessibility`: `failing` is a site of one page that breaks the rules of [Accessibility](../../docs/BEHAVIOUR.md#accessibility): text with enough contrast for level AA and not for AAA, text whose contrast fails in the dark colour scheme only, an image without a text alternative, links that Tab reaches out of order, and a block whose button Space does not turn over. The browser check, `tests/browser/accessibility.mjs`, must find each of them. Every other fixture that builds is checked too: that file lists which fixtures it builds, and which make no site.
- `step-sentences`: steps that try every part of what a sentence is and how sentences are grouped: quoted values, empty and unclosed, quotes just after a backslash, other quotation marks, outline placeholders, quoted or not, from two examples blocks, and `<` and `>` that are not placeholders, `<>` among them, in an outline with a column whose name is empty, numbers, a step in NFD, a step with a data table and one with a doc string, `And`, `But` and `*` steps, an `And` first in its scenario and one after a `*`, the same text in two kinds and in two cases, backgrounds of a feature and of a rule, a Portuguese step written as an English one, a feature in a folder beside a file whose name sorts between them as text, and a feature in Portuguese.
- `no-steps`: a feature whose only scenario has no step, and the page of step sentences its build writes, in `expected`.
- `search`: the input of search's documents, in `features`, with the documents expected of it in `search.json`: a feature with tags and a background, a scenario with a data table and a doc string, an outline whose examples blocks repeat a tag, a rule with its own background and tags, an unnamed scenario, a feature in Portuguese at the input's root, and a feature without a name, with an unnamed rule holding an outline whose examples repeat its tag, and a rule without scenarios. Its doc string and table hold words found nowhere else, to check they are not searched.
- `release`: the release tools, not a build. `before`, `since` and `later` hold commit messages, made into a throwaway repository with the tag `v0.1.0` after `before` and `v0.2.0` after `since`; `notes.md` is the section git-cliff must write for `v0.2.0`, and `notes-later.md`, with only a `Fixed` section, the one for the commits after it. `changelogs` holds the changelogs the release gate is tried with: one with notes for the version, one without its section, and one whose section is empty.
- `action`: the folder the GitHub Action's build runs in, with a `ghg.toml` that names `specs` as the input, beside a `features` folder that fails, read only when the action's `input` names it.

The cargo plugin, `cargo ghg`, is run over the `configuration` folders too, and checked to behave exactly as `ghg` does there.

The example suite of the project's own site, `project-site/features/`, is checked the same way, against "The project's own site".

Some files here are left out of git by the fixture's own `.gitignore`, on purpose, and were added with `git add --force`.
